      - article:
        - heading "Formula" [level=2]
        - paragraph: The nth roots of Re^(i theta) are
        - strong: z_k = R^(1/n)e^(i(theta + 360°k)/n)
        - paragraph: for k = 0, 1, 2, ..., n - 1.
        - separator
        - generic: Key ideas
        - paragraph:
          - text: ✓ Take the nth root of the modulus.
          - text: ✓ Divide the circle into n equal angles.
          - text: ✓ Add k = 0...n-1 to get all roots.
      - article:
        - heading "Worked example" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Find the fourth roots of 16.
        - paragraph:
          - text: • Write 16 = 16e^(i0°)
          - text: • n = 4 -> radius = 16^(1/4) = 2.
          - text: • Angle step = 360°/4 = 90°.
          - text: "• Roots:"
          - text: "k=0: 2"
          - text: "k=1: 2i"
          - text: "k=2: -2"
          - text: "k=3: -2i"
        - paragraph: These four points are equally spaced on the circle.
      - article:
        - heading "Practice challenge" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Find the cube roots of 8; predict the angle spacing first.

      - generic: ⚠ Common misconception
      - paragraph: A nonzero complex number has n nth-roots, not just one.
      - paragraph: All roots have the same distance from the origin but different angles. Only when n=1 do we get a single root.
